name: security-model-serving-batch-isolation-review
intent: Multi-tenant model-serving request and response isolation in batching
artifacts: Batch scheduler, request identity, KV/prefix cache, streaming routing and cancellation lifecycle.
trace: Trace tokens/outputs/state through dynamic batching and cache reuse to the correct caller, especially canceled/retried requests.
experiment: Use a local deterministic serving stub or owned isolated runtime with distinct synthetic prompt markers and bounded batches.
disproof: Semantically similar output is not cross-request leakage without attributed private marker/state; public model knowledge is not tenant data.
repair: Bind cache and stream ownership through batch lifecycle and verify canceled, retried and simultaneous entitled requests.
branch_decisions: Track request-to-output slots through dynamic batching, cancellation, streaming and KV/prefix cache reuse. Shared model weights and public prompt prefixes may be expected; private prompts, generated tokens and tenant-specific adapters have different isolation requirements. Use distinguishable synthetic tenants and observe final routing, not only an internal tensor allocation that cannot affect another request.
operational_method: Retain request ID, tenant, slot generation, cache provenance and final stream owner through admit, cancel, release and reallocate events. Compare cancellation of requestA followed by slot reuse for B with a legitimate same-tenant prefix-cache hit. The implementation trace must show which generation owns each emitted token/response; a toy scheduler demonstrates only its own behavior and cannot certify a real serving runtime or accelerator cache.
